neighbours.label: the token that closes a parenthetical aside (')', '),', closing dash) so the main clause can resume, versus the same content without an aside
fire: The new bridge (which took six years to build) finally opened on Monday.
Maria Lopez (born 1921) was a teacher in the mountain villages.
Older phones (which most families keep in a drawer) can be recycled for parts.
The council – which had promised lower taxes – raised fees again.
The museum's west wing (closed since the flood) will reopen next spring.
My first car (a rusty green hatchback) broke down every winter.
The treaty – signed in secret in 1839 – shaped the region for a century.
His latest album (recorded in a single week) has sold very well.
quiet: The new bridge finally opened on Monday after six years of building.
Maria Lopez was a teacher in the mountain villages for forty years.
Older phones can be recycled for parts instead of kept in a drawer.
The council had promised lower taxes but raised fees again.
The museum's west wing will reopen next spring after the flood.
My first car was a rusty green hatchback that broke down every winter.
The treaty was signed in secret in 1839 and shaped the region for a century.
His latest album was recorded in a single week and has sold very well.

predictions: closing ')' or dash of a mid-sentence aside 0.3+; the same sentences without the aside near 0
